caption_L1: Here a is a bar plot called Rate of new liver cancer diagnoses in the U.S. as of 2017 , by age (per 100,000 population). The x-axis shows Rate per 100,000 population with linear scale of range 0 to 40 while the y-axis measures Year as categorical scale starting with 1-4 years and ending with Less than 1 year.
caption_L2L3: The rate of diagnosis of liver cancer does not become than 10 per 100,000 head of population until the age of 50-54 years. From 50-54 years the rate steadily increases to the age of 80-84 years, where it is nearly 40 per 100,000 population. After the age of 85 the rate drops down significantly.
